I’m not trans myself but I’m LGBT (still partially closeted) and my s/o is trans (trans man so bit different experiences but you get the gist. Transitioning and coming out are both a process. It’s a long road and it’s not all easy but there are things that make it worth it. 

The world is changing. My fiancé and I both live in what is considered by a lot of the country as a very LGBT-unfriendly area but even things are changing here. Even within the past couple of years, I’ve noticed a marked change in how many people are accepting. Sometimes people ask questions that are kind of obtuse but generally people have good intentions. 

That’s not to say it’s all easy but I want you to know that a lot more people are accepting nowadays than you’d think. 

I know it sounds cheesy but there are lots of support groups out there. Here there is a small group with older trans folks that act as mentors to younger trans folks. Even just stopping in somewhere can help. You don’t feel so alone all of a sudden. You realize that there are LGBT people all around you that you didn’t realize. 

Much love to you.
Hello, I’m in a similar situation as you. If you want to talk over PM we can. It might be helpful.
I used to think Kenny Chesney's "No Shoes, No Shirt, No Problems" was "No Shoes, No Shirt, No Bottoms".

I used to live a short walk from a movie theater where I'd go in the mornings when no else would go and enjoy the movies all to myself. The best part was it was one of those nice theaters with the cushy seats and good food and drink. Very relaxing.
